messages:
beth_prod: Hey team — hitting weird embeddings errors in prod after a deploy. Some requests return 200 but embedding length is 1 (just a small array) and downstream code blows up. No schema change on our side. Any ideas?

alex_support: sorry you're seeing this — can you paste an example request/response (sanitized tokens) and the error you get?

beth_prod: here's a redacted snippet of the fetch we use (client JS):

```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACTED',
    // we forgot content-type earlier and then tried adding it 
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-embed-5', input: 'Customer text goes here' })
})
```

beth_prod: response we get:

```json
{
  "data": [ [0.0023] ],
  "model": "rw-embed-5",
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 3 }
}
```

beth_prod: so data[0] is a 1-dim vector (length 1), not 1536 like before. Also sometimes we see 400: "input must be an array" after toggling content-type.

alex_support: thanks. Two likely culprits: 1) sending a string instead of an array (singleton should be ["..."] not "..."), 2) double-stringifying or sending NDJSON/lines with wrong content-type. Can you try the payload as an array?

sam_eng: adding: when the client sends a bare string as JSON body ("input": "hello"), some server-side parsers interpret it as a scalar and the runtime falls back to returning a small default embedding (historical behavior) — that explains the length-1 vectors. Also if the client JSON is stringified twice you can end up sending a JSON string whose inner content looks like an array but is typed as string, e.g. body = JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify({input: [...] })) -> server sees input as a string.

beth_prod: ok repro steps I did: 1) removed content-type header, 2) sent body as JSON.stringify({model, input: 'hi'}) -> got length-1 embedding. 3) switched to JSON.stringify({model, input: ['hi']}) and added header 'Content-Type: application/json' -> got normal-length embedding.

sam_eng: perfect — that confirms client-side shape bug. For posterity, here's common broken vs correct JS patterns:

Broken (singleton string):
```js
body = JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-embed-5', input: 'hello' })
// server treats as scalar => fallback tiny vector or 400
```

Broken (double-stringified):
```js
body = JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-embed-5', input: ['hello'] }))
// Content-Type application/json but payload is a JSON string, server sees types wrong
```

Correct:
```js
body = JSON.stringify({ model: 'rw-embed-5', input: ['hello'] })
headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
```

alex_support: also note: if you send nested arrays like input: [["a"]] or input: [[0.1, 0.2]] the server may interpret that as a batch-of-vectors vs batch-of-strings and perform a different validation path — that leads to shape errors (dimension mismatch) if you mix string inputs and numeric vectors in same request. Keep input homogenous: either strings or numeric vectors of correct dim.

beth_prod: we had a mixed path in our batching pipeline where singletons were wrapped differently in different branches. Fixing to always ensure an array at the callsite fixed it.

alex_support: for immediate mitigation: 1) validate on client: Array.isArray(payload.input) and typeof payload.input[0] === 'string' 2) add a short middleware that normalizes singletons: if (!Array.isArray(input)) input = [input] 3) enable stricter server-side validation (we can flip a flag on your org to return 422 on scalar input instead of fallback) if you want.

beth_prod: can you flip that stricter validation for our org? We want it to fail fast.

alex_support: pinging infra-bot to request stricter-input-validation for org org_abc123. @infra-bot please create an ops ticket. :pray:

infra-bot: ops ticket created: OP-6321 — "Enable strict embeddings input validation for org_abc123". Assigned to eng-sam. ETA 2 business days.

sam_eng: I can do a quick patch to the validation layer: return 422 if input type !== array or if mixed element types. I'll add a canary rollout to a small percentage of requests for your org first. Will update in-thread when done.

beth_prod: thank you! one more ask: is there a best practice for batching many single items from the browser (we sometimes send one-by-one)? We saw a small billing spike when a client-side retry loop sent lots of tiny requests after getting length-1 vectors.

alex_support: recommend batching on the client (group up to 64 inputs per request) and use exponential backoff on 5xx/429. Also consider sending compact payloads (strings not arrays of tokens) and using our SDK which does normalization for you. We'll follow up with a short PR that shows client-side batching helper.

beth_prod: great, appreciate the help. I'll patch our frontend to normalize and batch, watch for OP-6321, and report back. :thumbsup:

alex_support: thanks — marking this thread resolved for now, reach out if OP-6321 changes behavior or you see regressions.
